questions.question: What is a view in Rails and how does it work?
questions.title: Rails Views
questions.direct_answer: A view is the presentation layer: it takes the @vars the controller set and turns them into HTML (or JSON). Views live in app/views/<controller>/<action>.html.erb and render by convention — PostsController#show renders app/views/posts/show.html.erb. ERB tags: <% %> runs Ruby (no output), <%= %> runs and outputs (escaped). Views should be dumb: just display the @vars, no queries or business logic (that's the model/controller). Partials (_form.html.erb, render 'form') and layouts (application.html.erb with yield) compose pages from shared pieces. For an API, render json: replaces the view entirely. The view's only job: present the data the controller gave it.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know a view renders @vars into HTML by convention (action view path), uses ERB, and stays dumb (no logic).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Putting queries or logic in the view (belongs in the model/controller), or not knowing the view path convention.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: A view presents the controller's @vars as HTML (or JSON). Renders by convention (app/views/posts/show.html.erb). ERB tags; views are dumb; partials/layouts compose pages.

sections.title: Controller @vars -> View
sections.content:
A view presents @vars as HTML by convention. ERB tags; partials/layouts compose; render json for APIs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[controller sets @vars] --> V[view: app/views/posts/show.html.erb]
  V --> E[ERB: <% %> / <%= %>]
  V --> P[partials + layout]
  V --> J[API: render json:]
```

sections.title: Views
sections.content:
```ruby # Controller sets @vars; the view presents them. class PostsController < ApplicationController def show @post = Post.find(params[:id]) # renders app/views/posts/show.html.erb by CONVENTION end end # app/views/posts/show.html.erb (the view; reads @post)

<%= @post.title %>

<%= @post.body %>

<% if @post.published? %> Published <% end %> <%= render 'form' %> # Views are DUMB: no queries, no business logic — just present @vars. ```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Putting queries or logic in the view — that's the model/controller's job.
Not knowing the view path convention (app/views/posts/show.html.erb for #show).
Using <% %> where you need output (nothing shows — use <%= %>).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A view is the presentation layer: it presents the controller's @vars as HTML (or JSON).
Views render by convention: PostsController#show -> app/views/posts/show.html.erb.
ERB tags: <% %> runs (no output), <%= %> runs + outputs (escaped by default).
Views are dumb: just display @vars; no queries or business logic (model/controller's job).
Partials + layouts compose pages; render json: replaces the view for an API.
